sources.title: GeeksforGeeks - Layers of the OSI Model
sources.claim: The Physical layer transmits raw bit streams over a physical medium.

sources.title: GeeksforGeeks - Layers of the OSI Model
sources.claim: The Data Link layer exchanges frames between nodes on the same link using MAC addresses.

sources.title: GeeksforGeeks - Layers of the OSI Model
sources.claim: The Network layer handles logical (IP) addressing and routing of packets between networks.

sources.title: GeeksforGeeks - Layers of the OSI Model
sources.claim: The Transport layer provides end-to-end delivery, segmentation, and reassembly.

sources.title: GeeksforGeeks - Layers of the OSI Model
sources.claim: The Session layer establishes, maintains, and terminates sessions between applications.

sources.title: GeeksforGeeks - Layers of the OSI Model
sources.claim: The Presentation layer translates data into a common format (encoding, compression, encryption).

sources.title: GeeksforGeeks - Layers of the OSI Model
sources.claim: The Application layer is associated with protocols such as HTTP, SMTP, and DNS.

rounds.prompt: Which of the following devices operates primarily at Layer 1 (Physical Layer) of the OSI model, dealing directly with raw electrical, optical, or radio signals?

choices.label: Router
choices.why: A router works at Layer 3: it forwards packets using IP addresses.

choices.label: Hub
choices.why: A hub repeats raw electrical signals out of every port without reading addresses or frames. That is Layer 1.

choices.label: Unmanaged Switch
choices.why: A switch reads the MAC address in each frame. That is Layer 2.

choices.label: Firewall
choices.why: A firewall inspects packets and sessions, which is Layer 3 and above.

rule.explanation: A hub only repeats signals, so it is a Layer 1 (Physical) device.

rounds.prompt: What is the primary data unit and core addressing mechanism used at Layer 2 (Data Link Layer) of the OSI model?

choices.label: Packets and IP addresses
choices.why: Packets and IP addresses belong to Layer 3 (Network).

choices.label: Segments and Port numbers
choices.why: Segments and port numbers belong to Layer 4 (Transport).

choices.label: Frames and MAC addresses
choices.why: Layer 2 sends frames between devices on the same link, addressed with MAC addresses.

choices.label: Bits and voltages
choices.why: Bits and voltages are Layer 1 (Physical).

rule.explanation: Layer 2 (Data Link) uses frames and MAC addresses.

rounds.prompt: Which networking device is most famously associated with Layer 3 (Network Layer) because it routes traffic across different networks using logical addresses?

choices.label: Network Hub
choices.why: A hub is a Layer 1 device; it does not route.

choices.label: Router
choices.why: A router forwards packets between networks using logical (IP) addresses. That is Layer 3.

choices.label: Repeater
choices.why: A repeater regenerates signals, which is Layer 1.

choices.label: Network Interface Card (NIC) in Promiscuous Mode
choices.why: A NIC works at Layers 1 and 2; promiscuous mode only lets it accept every frame it sees. It does not route.

rule.explanation: Routers use logical addresses to move packets between networks: Layer 3.

rounds.prompt: Which of the following protocols operates at Layer 4 (Transport Layer) and provides reliable, connection-oriented data transmission using a three-way handshake?

choices.label: UDP (User Datagram Protocol)
choices.why: UDP is also Layer 4, but it is connectionless: no handshake and no delivery guarantee.

choices.label: IP (Internet Protocol)
choices.why: IP is Layer 3 (Network).

choices.label: HTTP (Hypertext Transfer Protocol)
choices.why: HTTP is Layer 7 (Application).

choices.label: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol)
choices.why: TCP is a Layer 4 protocol that opens connections with a three-way handshake and delivers data reliably.

rule.explanation: TCP is the reliable, connection-oriented Layer 4 protocol.

rounds.prompt: What is the primary role of Layer 5 (Session Layer) in the OSI model?

choices.label: Translating character encodings and handling data compression
choices.why: Encoding and compression are Layer 6 (Presentation).

choices.label: Establishing, managing, and terminating communication dialogues between applications
choices.why: The Session layer sets up, maintains, and ends the dialogue between applications.

choices.label: Managing end-to-end flow control and port multiplexing
choices.why: Flow control and ports are Layer 4 (Transport).

choices.label: Providing a direct graphical user interface to end users
choices.why: A user interface belongs to the application itself (Layer 7 at most), not the Session layer.

rule.explanation: Layer 5 (Session) establishes, manages, and terminates sessions.

rounds.prompt: Which of the following functions is typically handled at Layer 6 (Presentation Layer) of the OSI model?

choices.label: Data translation, encryption/decryption, and compression
choices.why: Layer 6 makes sure both ends agree on data format: translation, encryption, and compression.

choices.label: Path selection and packet forwarding across routers
choices.why: Path selection and forwarding are Layer 3 (Network).

choices.label: Establishing TCP socket connections
choices.why: TCP connections are Layer 4 (Transport).

choices.label: Web browser rendering of HTML/CSS
choices.why: Rendering a page is done by the application (Layer 7).

rule.explanation: Layer 6 (Presentation) handles translation, encryption, and compression.

rounds.prompt: Which of the following protocols operates directly at Layer 7 (Application Layer) of the OSI model?

choices.label: TCP
choices.why: TCP is Layer 4 (Transport).

choices.label: IPv4
choices.why: IPv4 is Layer 3 (Network).

choices.label: Ethernet
choices.why: Ethernet covers Layers 1 and 2 (Physical and Data Link).

choices.label: HTTP
choices.why: HTTP is an application protocol: Layer 7.

boss.prompt: LAYER 8 BOSS. The switch lights are green, the pings are fine, and yet your boss has appeared at your cubicle with a coffee mug to ask if you got the memo about the new cover sheet for the TPS reports, and whether you could come in on Saturday. In network troubleshooting folklore, what is "Layer 8" of the OSI model?

choices.label: A premium firewall tier that automatically blocks every email beginning with "Per my last email"
choices.why: Nice idea, but Layer 8 is not a product or a device. Firewalls work at Layer 3 and up, and none of them can stop a manager with a mug.

choices.label: The printer, specifically the one that keeps saying PC LOAD LETTER
choices.why: A jammed printer is a driver or paper problem (Layer 7 and Layer 1), and it may deserve a field and a baseball bat, but it is not Layer 8.

choices.label: The people: users, managers, and office politics sitting above the seven real layers
choices.why: Correct: Layer 8 is the informal joke layer for the humans. The cable is fine, the humans are the problem.

choices.label: The fiber run to the basement, where they moved Milton and his red stapler
choices.why: Cabling is Layer 1, and relocating Milton to the basement does not create a new OSI layer, just a stapler grievance.

rule.explanation: Layer 8 is an informal joke, not part of the OSI model: the people above the seven real layers (users, managers, and office politics). When every layer checks out and things are still broken, check Layer 8, and maybe bring a second copy of the cover sheet.
